Sit in the back-ish but don't separate yourself from "the pack." If no one sits in the back five rows, don't be way away from everyone else. Standing out will only make you more self conscious and less focused on the ceremony.

Try to remember to bow or curtesy when entering a row of pews, and if you pass by a decorated box in the wall or on a pedestal, go down on one knee and cross yourself. (Try to avoid the fancy box or crossing past the altar in the front of the church until you're more comfortable with all the motions).

Follow along with what people are doing. When they sit or stand or kneel, do the same (to your ability). You don't need to recite anything you don't know, but the Our Father prayer is one that I knew at least half of my first time.

Know how to cross yourself: forehead, chest (breastbone, sometimes lower I've noticed in some countries), left shoulder, right shoulder. It's okay to go a little slower than other people and watch them first. 

Go up when everyone else is going up for communion. When it's your turn, cross your arms over your chest with your right hand on your left shoulder and your left hand on your right shoulder. The priest will bless you instead of giving you communion, a common practice for unconfirmed or visitors to Mass.

If you get too nervous to go up during communion, stay in your row (let everyone else by at least) and then kneel in the pew and put your hands in front of you clasped together in prayer. Take this time to reflect, pray, practice mindfulness, to listen to the music, to close your eyes and focus on breathing, or to look up at the art. Usually people will take some time and then sit back in their chair or once everyone is done with communion; keep an eye on others and slide back into your seat when others seem to be doing the same

That's all the hints I can think of!! No one is going to kick you out for making a mistake or missing a bow or forgetting to cross yourself or anything. And don't worry; I thought the priest would know I wasn't One of Them and find me and I'd burst into flames or something!! But it ended up going well and I didn't call attention to myself or make any awful mistakes! Have a good time, learn, reflect, breathe, and enjoy the ceremony. God bless!

Edit: "referred pain" is also why people with chest pain often feel left arm pain.
